235076.title: Busan Fireworks Festival
235076.overview: Korea's largest fireworks display, fired over the water at Gwangalli with the Gwangan Bridge itself as part of the set — the bridge's lighting rig is choreographed into the show alongside the pyrotechnics and a music score. It began in 2005 as a celebration for the APEC summit held in Busan and is now in its 21st year, drawing crowds well into the hundreds of thousands. Viewing spreads along Gwangalli Beach, across to Haeundae and around Igidae. Paid seating is sold for the main viewing areas; the beach fills early, so arrive hours ahead or watch from Igidae for a wider angle.
235076.fee: Paid seating (free viewing from surrounding areas)

506909.title: Jindo Miracle Sea Road Festival
506909.overview: Twice a year the tide drops far enough to expose a 2.8 km strip of seabed between Hoedong-ri and the island of Modo, and for about an hour people walk across the sea on a path 30–40 m wide. It is designated Scenic Site No. 9. The phenomenon became internationally known in 1975, when the French ambassador to Korea — visiting to see the Jindo dog — witnessed it and described it in the French press as a modern parting of the Red Sea; a 1996 Japanese hit song about it still brings Japanese visitors every year. The festival programmes Jindo's intangible heritage alongside the crossing: Jindo Arirang, ganggangsullae circle dance, ssitgimgut shamanic rites, and Jindo drum dance. Free. The crossing window is tide-dependent and lasts about an hour — check the exact time before travelling.

2828431.title: Hangang Festival
2828431.overview: Seoul's summer programme on the Han River, spread across the riverside parks. Events include a raft race in homemade boats to pick fruit hung over the water, all-night screenings of nostalgic summer dramas and horror films with late-night food, jazz and K-pop concerts, a drone show flying over the river surface, DJ sets and hip-hop at an infinity pool overlooking the skyline, and traditional tightrope walking staged at a swimming area. There is a cinema under a bridge, a water picnic with activities for families at Seoul Battleship Park, silent-disco DJ parties and yoga with headsets, an overnight Han River walk now in its tenth year, and paddleboards, kayaks, yachts and cruises on the water. Mostly free, with some programmes charged.
2828431.place: Mangwon Hangang Park, Seoul Battleship Park and other riverside sites

1100492.title: Goyang Lake Arts Festival
1100492.overview: A street-arts festival held around Ilsan Lake Park, one of the largest artificial lake parks in Asia. Around 100 performances run across the park — circus, magic, aerial work and pieces that sit between genres — alongside hands-on programmes open to anyone. Fireworks over the lake and night-time programming close each evening. Free, and about 40 minutes from central Seoul on Subway Line 3.
1100492.place: Ilsan Lake Park and Ilsan Culture Plaza

140897.title: Gyeongsan Gatbawi Wish Fulfillment Festival
140897.overview: Gatbawi is a 9th-century stone Buddha near the summit of Palgongsan, wearing a flat slab on its head that looks like a traditional Korean hat — hence the name. It has drawn people praying for a single wish to be granted for over a thousand years, and this festival, now in its 25th year, is built around that. The two days include a yadanbeopseok gathering mixing rock bands, Buddhist chant, Wonhyo's muae dance and sound meditation; an opening bibimbap offering shared among the crowd; a healing concert with gugak singer Nam Sang-il; and an orchestral wish concert with baritone Kim Dong-gyu and soprano Kang Hye-jung. A temple run along the Gatbawi wish trail and a templestay at Seonbonsa run on advance registration, and there are temple-food demonstrations and wish-paper hanging at the main site. Free.

981658.title: Daejeon Hyo Culture Roots Festival
981658.overview: Hyo — filial devotion to one's parents and ancestors — is the organising idea of this festival, held in Ppuri Park, a hillside park in Daejeon planted with sculpted stones representing the origin of Korean family clans. Visitors can trace the history of a surname and its clan lineage, and the programme wraps that in traditional performances and hands-on activities aimed at getting several generations of a family taking part together. Free.

2612274.title: Gwanak Gang Gam-chan Festival
2612274.overview: Gang Gam-chan commanded the Goryeo army that destroyed a Khitan invasion force at Gwiju in 1019, one of the decisive victories in Korean history. He was born in what is now Gwanak-gu in southern Seoul, at a spot called Nakseongdae — 'the place where a star fell', after the legend that a star dropped there at his birth — and the festival is staged in the park built around it. It began in 2016 by merging two older local events, an azalea festival running since 1998 and a memorial rite since 1988. The 2026 edition marks ten years. Free.

2558866.title: Yesan Market Samguk Festival
2558866.overview: Samguk here is a pun: the three 'guk' of Yesan are gukbap (rice soup), guksu (noodles) and gukhwa (chrysanthemums). The festival takes over Yesan's permanent market, which has become one of the better-known market redevelopments in Korea. 2026 marks both the festival's tenth year and the market's hundredth, and the programme is built around food stalls, chrysanthemum displays and collaborations with young local makers. Free.

3522322.title: Oh Slow Vintage Market
3522322.overview: A vintage and antique market at Incheon Art Platform, a cluster of restored 1930s warehouses in the old open-port quarter — which makes the setting as much of the draw as the stalls. Dealers from across the country bring vintage clothing, antique objects, retro homeware and handmade pieces, with busking, DJ sets and photo zones alongside. Free.

506516.title: Daegu Yangnyeongsi Herbal Medicine Festival
506516.overview: Yangnyeongsi has been Daegu's herbal medicine market since 1658 — 367 years — and remains the largest in the country, a dense grid of streets where the smell of dried roots and bark carries for blocks. The festival opens the market up with traditional-medicine programmes, performances and hands-on sessions built around a time-slip theme. Entry is free; a few activities charge up to 3,000 won.
506516.fee: Free entry (some activities up to 3,000 won)

141661.title: Royal Guard-Changing Ceremony at Gyeongbokgung Palace
141661.overview: The sumungun were the soldiers who held the gates of the Joseon palaces, and this reenactment has run at Gyeongbokgung since 2002. It was reconstructed from a record in the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty describing the gate-guard system introduced in 1469, and the costumes and weapons are reproductions of early-Joseon military kit. The ceremony proper runs at 10:00 and 14:00 in the plaza in front of Heungnyemun Gate; a separate gate-sentry ceremony runs at Gwanghwamun at 11:00 and 13:00, and there is an open guard drill at 09:35 and 13:35. All of it is free and outside the ticket gate, so you can watch without paying palace admission. Cancelled in heavy rain and on Tuesdays, when the palace closes.
141661.place: Heungnyemun Gate Plaza and Gwanghwamun, Gyeongbokgung Palace
141661.hours: Guard changing 10:00 and 14:00 · Gate sentry ceremony 11:00 and 13:00 · Open drill 09:35 and 13:35
141661.sponsor: Korea Heritage Service, Royal Palaces and Tombs Center
